Redesign how Nxeon's plans and BILLING TERMS are presented so they look premium, differentiate clearly, and actively upsell customers into BIGGER plans and LONGER terms. Also fix a price-display bug. Work EXCLUSIVELY in /opt/nxeon-wt-pricingredesign (branch feature/pricing-plan-term-redesign). node_modules symlinked. Do NOT run build/prisma commands — code only. This is MARKETING/UX + display: ALL prices stay DB-fed (db.plan/hostingPlan/emailPlan/gamePlan) — never hardcode a price and never change what's charged. The owner's exact complaint: "all of the plans just said $2.99 — confusing. Restructure how plans AND terms are shown to look more appealing and provoke people into getting bigger/longer terms. We also need the pricing page overhaul."

DIAGNOSE + FIX THE PRICE BUG FIRST:
- VPS plans are $6.49/$8.99/$12.99/$20.99/$32.99; shared hosting is $2.99/$4.99/$8.99. Somewhere VPS (or the product picker) shows "$2.99" — likely the hosting first-month-free PromoBar and/or the homepage product-picker's "from" price bleeding hosting's $2.99 onto the VPS/Game tabs. Grep the marketing surfaces (components/marketing/ProductPricing.tsx, PricingBar/PromoBar.tsx, app/page.tsx, app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx, PricingGrid.tsx, PricingNav.tsx). Ensure EACH product's "from" price is its OWN minimum (VPS from $6.49, Game from its min, Hosting from $2.99) — no cross-product leakage. Ensure the PromoBar's "$2.99" is clearly a HOSTING message, not something that reads as an all-plans price. Every plan card must show its own distinct real price, prominently.

REDESIGN THE PLAN DISPLAY (make plans look premium + differentiated + upsell to bigger):
- On /vps, /pricing, the homepage product section, and the customer deploy wizard: give each tier a clear identity (name, target user, headline specs), a prominent distinct price, a visible "Most popular" anchor on a mid/high tier, and a subtle "best value"/"most resources" cue on the top tier. Use price anchoring (show the biggest plan's value) so the mid-tier feels like the smart buy. Keep the navy+violet+cyan design system, Reveal animations, and existing components — elevate them, don't rebuild from scratch.

REDESIGN THE TERM DISPLAY (the core ask — provoke LONGER terms):
- VPS supports Monthly/Annual/2-year/3-year; hosting/email/game/NxCloud now support Monthly/Annual (built recently — study lib/billing-terms.ts termPriceCents + the term selectors in DeployWizard.tsx / HostingClient / EmailHosting / GameDeploy / NxcloudClient / the /pricing hub).
- Make the term selector a persuasive ladder: for each longer term show the effective **$/mo**, the **% saved vs monthly**, the **total saved over the term** (e.g. "Save $XX/yr"), and a "Best value"/"Save most" badge on the longest term. Default-highlight ANNUAL (not monthly) as the recommended choice, with monthly clearly available. Make picking a longer term feel like the obviously smart move (real numbers from termPriceCents + the annual_discount_percent setting — truthful, never invented). If only Monthly+Annual exist for a product, show both compellingly; where 2yr/3yr exist (VPS), show the full ladder with increasing savings.
- Reflect the chosen term consistently (price shown = price charged; the money logic is already built — you're only improving presentation).

PRICING PAGE OVERHAUL (/pricing):
- Deliver the polished multi-product hub the owner wants: clear product switcher, per-product comparison with the redesigned plan cards, the persuasive term ladder, a "which is right for me" chooser, honest trust row, consistent /register CTAs. Make it look like a premium host's pricing page (Hostinger/Vultr-class) — appealing, scannable, conversion-oriented. First-month-free shown on SHARED HOSTING only (don't reintroduce it on VPS). No fabricated numbers.

Keep it truthful and DB-fed throughout. DELIVER, then commit `git add -A && git commit -m "feat(marketing): premium plan + term presentation (upsell longer terms) + fix VPS $2.99 leak + /pricing overhaul"` (trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>), `git push -u origin feature/pricing-plan-term-redesign`. REPORT (factual): the $2.99 bug root cause + fix, the plan-card redesign, the term-ladder design (what savings cues you show + that annual is default-highlighted), the /pricing overhaul, and confirm every price is DB-fed with nothing fabricated. Don't claim tested.

1	/**
2	 * Billing term definitions + discount math, shared by ordering, renewal,
3	 * the deploy wizard, invoices and the domain flow. Discounts are the platform's
4	 * promo (longer commitment = cheaper); tune here (or later via admin Settings).
5	 */
6	
7	export type VpsTerm = { months: number; label: string; short: string; discountPct: number };
8	
9	/** The ANNUAL term is 12 months — the one term whose discount is admin-configurable. */
10	export const ANNUAL_TERM_MONTHS = 12;
11	
12	/**
13	 * The annual (12-month) commitment discount SHIPPED as the default, and the fallback
14	 * for the `annual_discount_percent` admin setting (lib/annual-discount.ts).
15	 *
16	 * It MUST equal the 12-month `VPS_TERMS` discountPct below: a platform whose
17	 * `Setting` table has no `annual_discount_percent` row must price the annual term
18	 * EXACTLY as it did before the setting existed, so no existing annual server's
19	 * renewal price moves the moment this wiring lands. The setting only ever raises or
20	 * lowers it deliberately, from the admin Billing panel.
21	 */
22	export const DEFAULT_ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PCT = 10;
23	
24	export const VPS_TERMS: VpsTerm[] = [
25	  { months: 1, label: "Monthly", short: "1 mo", discountPct: 0 },
26	  // Annual is admin-configurable — this is only the SHIPPED default. Every charge
27	  // path resolves the live rate via `annualDiscountPct()` and passes it through
28	  // `vpsTermPriceCents`; this constant is what an un-wired caller (and a 2-arg call)
29	  // falls back to. Keep it === DEFAULT_ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PCT.
30	  { months: 12, label: "Annual", short: "1 yr", discountPct: DEFAULT_ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PCT },
31	  { months: 24, label: "Biennial", short: "2 yr", discountPct: 15 },
32	  { months: 36, label: "Triennial", short: "3 yr", discountPct: 20 },
33	];
34	
35	export function vpsTerm(months: number): VpsTerm {
36	  return VPS_TERMS.find((t) => t.months === months) ?? VPS_TERMS[0];
37	}
38	
39	/**
40	 * The discount percent to apply to a term.
41	 *
42	 * For the ANNUAL (12-month) term this is admin-configurable: pass the
43	 * `annualDiscountPct` resolved from the `annual_discount_percent` setting
44	 * (lib/annual-discount.ts) and it WINS over the shipped default. Every other term
45	 * keeps its fixed `VPS_TERMS` rate. Omitting the override — or passing a
46	 * non-finite value — falls back to the shipped default, so a 2-arg
47	 * `vpsTermPriceCents` call and any caller that has not been wired up price annual at
48	 * `DEFAULT_ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PCT`, i.e. exactly what the platform shipped before.
49	 * Clamped to 0..90 here as a second line of defence behind the setting reader.
50	 */
51	export function termDiscountPct(months: number, annualDiscountPct?: number): number {
52	  if (months === ANNUAL_TERM_MONTHS && annualDiscountPct != null && Number.isFinite(annualDiscountPct)) {
53	    return Math.min(90, Math.max(0, annualDiscountPct));
54	  }
55	  return vpsTerm(months).discountPct;
56	}

Done. Committed and pushed to `feature/pricing-plan-term-redesign`. Clean typecheck (`tsc --noEmit` exit 0, no errors in any touched file). Not run in the app — not tested.

## The $2.99 bug — root cause + fix
There was no VPS card literally printing $2.99; the confusion came from two real hosting-price leaks that read as an all-plans price:

1. **Sitewide `PromoBar`** (`components/marketing/PromoBar.tsx`) renders at the very top of *every* marketing page — including `/vps`. It showed "Web hosting — … then $2.99/mo", so a visitor on the VPS page saw "$2.99/mo" as the first thing on screen. It's DB-fed from the cheapest `hostingPlan`, but the framing was weak. Fixed: it now leads with a bold **"Shared Hosting"** pill, reads "**Shared web hosting from $X/mo**", is emerald-themed (not the brand gradient that blended into product pricing), and links to `/web-hosting`. The $2.99 can no longer be misread as a VPS/all-plans price. Still 100% DB-fed.
2. **Hardcoded `"$2.99"` fallback** in `app/page.tsx` (`hostFrom = … : "$2.99"`) — an actual hardcoded price literal, injected into a homepage "Small businesses" tag. Removed: now `hostFromCents` is DB-derived and the price chip is simply omitted when no hosting plan exists (no invented number).

I also verified every "from" price is its own product's minimum: `ProductPricing` computes `from` per-selected-tab from that product's tiers only; `/pricing`'s overview derives each row from its own catalogue query. No cross-product leakage remains.

## Plan-card redesign (premium + differentiated + anchoring)
- **`/vps` (`PricingGrid`)**: top (most-expensive) tier now carries a **"Best value / Most resources"** anchor while the mid tier keeps **"Most popular"** — classic anchoring so the mid tier reads as the smart buy. Each card shows a real DB-fed annual `$/mo` line ("or $X/mo billed annually — save Y%") and a footer that states the from→top range and the annual saving. Now receives the live `annualDiscountPct` from the page.
- **Homepage (`ProductPricing`)**: product highlight badge fixed (was a misleading product-level "Most popular"; now a product-identity chip), added a from→top range line, a **"Best value · most resources"** cue on the top tier, and a nudge to `/pricing` for longer terms.
- **`/pricing` VPS table**: column headers now badge the mid plan "Most popular" and the top plan "Best value".

## Term-ladder redesign (the core ask — provoke longer terms)
Built one shared **`components/customer/TermLadder.tsx`** used by all four Monthly+Annual flows (Shared Hosting, Business Email, Game, NxCloud). For each term it shows: effective **$/mo** (with the monthly price struck through), **−X% off**, **total billed**, and **total saved** ("Save $X/yr"). The longest discounted term gets a **"Best value"** ribbon; annual gets **"Recommended"** where a longer term outranks it. **Annual is now the pre-selected default** in all four flows (was monthly) — monthly stays one click away and is labelled "Flexible — cancel anytime".

The VPS `DeployWizard` keeps its richer ladder (it layers first-term promo + per-term add-ons) but gained matching **"Recommended"** (annual) and **"Save most"** (3-year) ribbons, emerald-tinted borders, and punchier "Save $X vs monthly" copy. Its pre-selected term still honours the admin `default_term` setting (I deliberately didn't override an admin-owned value); the ribbons supply the "recommend annual" nudge.

`/pricing` also gained a worked **four-term VPS ladder** (computed on the entry plan, fully labelled) plus consistent "Pay yearly and save X%" notes on the hosting and email sections.

## Truthful + DB-fed
Every price flows from `db.plan/hostingPlan/emailPlan/gamePlan` through the existing `termPriceCents` formula with the live `annualDiscountPct()` — the same math checkout charges and renewals bill, so displayed = charged. No price is hardcoded anywhere (the one hardcoded `$2.99` fallback was removed), and no savings/discount number is invented — all are functions of the catalogue and the admin discount setting. First-month-free remains scoped to shared hosting only; it was not reintroduced on VPS.
